change_summary: The journal has retracted "Caffeine improves working memory in adults". An institutional investigation found that the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated, and the notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The stored paper's results section presents Figures 2 to 4 as showing accuracy by dose, so its headline accuracy finding rests on the fabricated figures. The authors have not responded.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The stored paper reports that 200 mg caffeine improved n-back accuracy by 12% compared with placebo. The journal has retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 were fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. This is the only citation of it, but it is the stated reason for your dose, so the impact on your draft is high.
recommendation: Remove or replace the citation to Brown and Kim [3] in the Introduction, because the journal has retracted the article and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Also re-check the 12% claim your draft uses as the reason for the 200 mg dose.
